title: Putin's Russia
subtitle: Since 1999
subject: comprendreLeMonde
description: In 25 years, a former KGB officer turned a country in crisis into an authoritarian power. A portrait of **Vladimir Putin** and his regime.

hero.hook: In 1999, almost nobody knew his name. Twenty-five years later, he has never left power.

blocks.text: Since he reached the top of the Russian state in 1999, **Vladimir Putin** has transformed the country. In a quarter of a century, he turned a nation weakened by the collapse of the USSR into a centralized, warlike power that openly defies the international order.

His rule followed a striking arc. Seen at first as a pragmatic stabilizer, he became the builder of an authoritarian system founded on control of energy, the crushing of all opposition, and a nostalgic vision of Russian imperial greatness.

Vladimir Putin's rise cannot be separated from the chaos of the 1990s. A former officer of the **[[KGB and FSB]]**, the Soviet and then Russian secret services, he learned his trade in Saint Petersburg before joining President Boris Yeltsin's circle in Moscow.
Vladimir Putin was almost unknown to the Russian public until August 1999, polling at 2%. Terrorist bombings and the war in Chechnya pushed him to 80% within a few months.

Elected president in March 2000, he built his term on an unspoken bargain: order would return and living standards would rise, in exchange for a gradual surrender of political freedom. Carried by soaring oil prices, Russian GDP grew eightfold between 1999 and 2008.

Once stability was won, Putin neutralized every independent center of power. He began by taming the **[[oligarchs]]**, the businessmen who had grown rich during the chaotic privatizations of the Yeltsin years. The signal came in 2003 with the arrest of Mikhail Khodorkovsky, the head of a large oil company.

The regime also went after press freedom. Television channels passed under the control of state companies such as Gazprom, turning news into propaganda. The opposition leader Alexei Navalny embodied the challenge from within: poisoned in 2020, he was jailed on his return, and he died in a penal colony in February 2024.
Although his official salary is modest, Vladimir Putin is often seen wearing luxury watches worth far more than his declared income.

The structure of the state itself drifted toward a system run by the **[[siloviki]]**, the men who come out of the armed forces and the secret services. They hold the key posts in the administration and in the big state companies, fusing security and financial interests around Putin's clan.

sections.title: Toward a break with the West

blocks.text: Putin's geopolitical vision rests on one trauma: the end of the USSR, which he called “the greatest geopolitical catastrophe of the 20th century.” His foreign policy aims to restore a zone of influence around Russia, opposing the expansion of NATO, which he treats as an act of aggression.

The escalation took physical form: Georgia in 2008, then 2014, when Russia illegally annexed Crimea and backed an armed insurgency in eastern Ukraine, the Donbas. Those acts marked the return of territorial war to Europe.

blocks.caption: Vladimir Putin has led Russia since 1999, first as president, then as prime minister, then as president again

blocks.text: The full invasion of Ukraine, launched on February 24, 2022, tipped Russia into a complete break with the West. It triggered the heaviest economic sanctions in modern history and, paradoxically, welded European and transatlantic unity back together against the Russian threat.

sections.title: The regime's ideology and its grip on power

blocks.text: To justify this confrontation, the Kremlin built a doctrine called [[“Sovereign democracy”]]: a specifically Russian path, grounded in conservative values, set against a West it judges decadent. The regime rewrites history, glorifying the victory of 1945 and playing down Stalin's crimes.

Putin locked in his hold on power with a constitutional reform in 2020 that in theory lets him stay president until 2036, while “foreign agent” laws are used to wipe out the last **civil society** organizations.

Putin came to power in 1999 promising stability. In twenty-five years, he rebuilt a strong state, silenced the opposition and turned Russia into a warlike authoritarian regime bent on violently overturning the world order.
